quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: Can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
Cannot turn anymore and must go straight.
Still have the right to turn without yielding.
Do not have to turn in the arrow's direction anymore.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Can be moving or in one place.
Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require you to slow down or pay attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be moving or in one place.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as vehicles that stripe lines, mow, or remove snow. Work zones use orange signs with black letters or symbols. Always slow down and stay alert when you see a work zone.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will come next.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light tells you that a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In the sun.
In the shade.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the shade.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, shaded areas freeze faster than other parts of the road. Shaded areas are also the last to dry. Drive with extra care on roads under trees or buildings.

questions.question: Pedestrians must yield to cars:

options.text: When crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection.
When crossing in a marked crosswalk.
When the car is a pickup truck.
Only in cities.

questions.correctAnswerText: When crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians must yield to cars when crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection. They must also yield when a traffic signal tells them to.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, you should:

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go when the first train passes.
Go when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, wait until you can see all tracks clearly before crossing. Do not move as soon as a train passes. Even with one track, check again for another train that may be coming.

questions.question: When another car is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to let them pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating and there is a right lane, move over. If there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slow down gradually. This gives them room to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road during dangerous conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed on a road during good conditions.
The suggested speed on a road during good conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road during good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed on a road during good conditions. You can drive slower, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or bad weather.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down so you can listen for a train.
Only continue if a flagger tells you it is safe.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow all their instructions.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use only your parking lights.
Use only your headlights.
Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When you stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on. This helps other drivers see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your reactions slow down.
You feel less confident.
Your body breaks it down faster.
You make fewer driving errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your reactions slow down.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more driving errors.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your turn signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: While driving, your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force your vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and gradually steer back onto the pavement.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down by gently pressing the brakes. When you are going slowly enough, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not make sharp turns.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal your lane change first. Then check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving into the new lane.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must make many decisions while driving. Any task that takes your attention away from the road is dangerous. Keep your full focus on driving.

questions.question: What authority do state and local authorities have over speed limits?

options.text: They must post the same speed limit for all similar roads.
They can change speed limits by posting signs in specific areas.
They cannot post different speed limits.
They must never post a speed limit lower than 35 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can change speed limits by posting signs in specific areas.
questions.explanation: State and local authorities can set different speed limits for different areas by posting speed limit signs. Follow the posted speed limit when it is reasonable and safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass the motorcycle while staying in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the same rights as other vehicles on the road. Give a motorcycle a full lane width. Even though it may look like there is room to share a lane, motorcycles need space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What is your blind spot?

options.text: The area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
The area you see in your rearview mirror.
The area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet make roads slippery. When road conditions are bad, you may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs indicate:

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Do not try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid crashes.
Defending yourself against bad drivers by passing them in traffic.
Following the car ahead of you very closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you watch for dangerous situations and act before a crash happens. It helps you stay safe from aggressive, careless, distracted, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning left. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down gradually. On a road with multiple lanes, move to the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
The road ahead curves to the left, then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn you about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Move as far off the road as possible to a safe location where other drivers can see you. Raise your hood to show your car is disabled.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Make eye contact with the driver as they pass.
Speed up while they are passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver is behind you, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact with them. Speeding up may anger them more and make things more dangerous.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so others know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill section is coming.

questions.question: Highway signs that warn drivers about dangerous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about hazards ahead. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them can cause accidents.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
Exiting an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, or when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When driving in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle has enough space to cross the tracks without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle has enough space to cross the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when you have an opening.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not immediately use your brakes.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: During a tire blowout, release the gas pedal and do not brake immediately. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, use your signal and enter at the same speed as other vehicles. Always yield to existing traffic.

questions.question: An arrow painted on the pavement means:

options.text: Drivers may make the movement shown by the arrow if they choose.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers must always stop before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road means drivers in that lane must move in the direction shown. Follow any traffic signs or signals before proceeding in that direction.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Side road.
Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It means an obstacle like a traffic island, median, or barrier is ahead. Stay on the side the arrow shows.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and make your turn there.
Safely change lanes, then put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and make your turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, continue to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: When making a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you start to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before a right turn, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cross other lanes to make your turn.
